history.dynasty: Modern — established 1967-68 by labour leader Pt. Parma Nand Tripathi; managed by the Shree Ram Mandir Trust
history.summary: The historic Rama temple of Bokaro Steel City, in Sector 1 near the post office — one of the major Hindu pilgrimage sites of Bokaro, Jharkhand. Established in 1967-68 by labour leader Pt. Parma Nand Tripathi, it is managed by the Shree Ram Mandir Trust, which organises around 250 low-cost marriages for poor families every year (one source says up to 300). Around the main Rama shrine the campus holds smaller temples of Hanuman, Radha-Krishna, Shiv Parivar, Durga, Surya, Kali, Lord Venkateshwar, Shiva and Sheetala, plus a rishi niwas and a religious library. The market near the temple is the oldest market of Bokaro, famed for its coffee house and street food (samosa, chaat, batata puri, phucka, rolls). IDENTITY NOTE (verify): a separate online listing titled 'Jai Sri Ram Mandir' at Sector 9/B near Patel Chowk repeats this same 1967 history text — it is likely a duplicate/listing conflation rather than a second 1967 temple; this file documents the Sector 1 temple.

name: Ram Mandir
town_description: Bokaro Steel City is a planned industrial city in Bokaro district, Jharkhand, built around the Bokaro Steel Plant — one of India's first public-sector steel plants, commissioned in the 1960s with Soviet collaboration. The city is laid out in numbered sectors with broad avenues, parks and markets, and draws settlers from across India, which is reflected in its temples representing many regional traditions. Nearby attractions include Garga Dam, the Parasnath Hills (a major Jain pilgrimage site) and the Rajrappa Chhinnamasta temple.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi — about 120 km from Bokaro Steel City (verify).
travel.railway: Bokaro Steel City railway station (BKSC) is the nearest major railhead; the temple at Sector 1 is about 1.3 km from it per a nearby-address listing (verify).
travel.road: Sector 1 (near the post office / Sector 1 market), in the heart of Bokaro Steel City; easily reached by city transport from anywhere in the township (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Ram Navami (Mar-Apr) is the grandest festival.
